papers.title: Sex and Gender Reporting and Female Participation Relative to Disease Burden in ClinicalTrials.gov
papers.abstract: Importance: Assessing representation by sex assigned at birth and gender identity requires reporting of both in trials. If disclosure of full gender and sex participation from clinicaltrials.gov is limited, it poses challenges in characterization and understanding of those participant experiences. Objective: To determine how often ClinicalTrials.gov trials published trials report sex and gender, which characteristics are associated with reporting, and how participants' female share compares with that of the general public. Design, Setting, and Participants: Cross-sectional study of interventional trials registered to ClinicalTrials.gov, with or without US sites, with primary completion on or after September 27, 2008, and results first posted from January 1, 2009, through April 30, 2026. Exposures: Funder type, phase, US sites, enrollment, primary completion year, number of countries, and therapeutic area. Main Outcomes and Measures: Reporting of sex and gender, and the female participation-to-prevalence ratio (PPR; trial female share divided by the number of people with the condition). Results: Among 58,007 trials (median enrollment, 72 [IQR, 31 to 206]; 42,644 [74%] with US sites), 553 (0.95%) reported gender and 57,683 (99.44%) reported sex. Gender reporting was more common with National Institutes of Health (NIH) funding (odds ratio [OR], 9.05; 95% CI, 6.65 to 12.6), US sites (OR, 4.21; 95% CI, 2.96 to 6.22), and larger enrollment. Across 10 conditions (15,552 mixed-sex trials), median PPR ranged from 0.68 (95% CI, 0.64 to 0.71) for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease to 1.05 (95% CI, 1.01 to 1.09) for obesity and had a relatively lower female share in 8. Among the 10 conditions most prevalent in our cohort, 6,917 of 16,097 trial condition combinations (43.0%) reached a PPR of at least 0.90; odds of reaching it were higher for NIH-funded (OR, 1.22; 95% CI, 1.11 to 1.34) and lower for government-funded trials (OR, 0.26; 95% CI, 0.20 to 0.33) as compared to industry-funded trials. Conclusions and Relevance: In ClinicalTrials.gov, sex reporting is nearly universal, whereas gender reporting is concentrated among NIH-funded, US-based, and larger trials. Female trial enrollment fell below the female share of people with the condition for most conditions, emphasizing the benefit of condition-specific benchmarks in clinical trials.

papers.title: Wastewater metagenomic sequencing quantitatively tracks transmission dynamics for human pathogenic viruses
papers.abstract: Wastewater metagenomic sequencing theoretically characterizes all nucleic acids in a sample, but whether sequencing reads reflect transmission dynamics of circulating viruses in the contributing community is unknown. We evaluated if wastewater metagenomic sequencing data can be used to reconstruct transmission dynamics of endemic, routinely circulating viruses. Using deep, untargeted wastewater metagenomic sequencing data from four locations in the United States, we generated quantitative estimates of transmission dynamics (time-varying growth rate and effective reproduction number) within a Bayesian framework for widely monitored viruses. Across locations and viruses, estimates were statistically concordant with those derived from clinical surveillance and polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-based wastewater monitoring data. Furthermore, we estimated growth rate from wastewater metagenomic sequencing data for numerous viruses not otherwise widely monitored, demonstrating the data expands the targets that can feasibly be monitored in parallel. Wastewater metagenomic sequencing can support both novel pathogen detection and routine surveillance of endemic pathogens.

papers.title: Chatbot as an intervention on physical activity: A systematic review and meta-analysis with meta-regression
papers.abstract: Background: Chatbots offer scalable, accessible, and personalized support for physical activity (PA). This review synthesized evidence on their efficacy and examined potential moderators. Methods: Eleven databases were searched for English-language published through January 27, 2026. Eligibility was assessed using the PICOS framework. Data extraction was guided by the research questions, mERA checklist, and PRISMA 2020. Risk of bias was evaluated using Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool and the NIH Quality Assessment Tool. Meta-analyses reported Hedges' g. Publication bias was evaluated using funnel plots, Egger's regression, and trim-and-fill analyses. Potential moderators were examined through subgroup analyses and meta-regression. Results: A total of 12,481 records were identified, of which 43 studies were included in the systematic review and 27 in the meta-analysis. Most studies included in the meta-analysis had some risk-of-bias concerns (16/27). Chatbot interventions produced a significant small-to-moderate post-intervention effect on PA (g = 0.31, 95% CI [0.19, 0.44]; n = 24), whereas the follow-up effect was small and non-significant (g = 0.11, 95% CI [-0.01, 0.22]; n = 4). Effects varied across PA outcomes (g = 0.08-0.44), and several subgroup differences helped explain the significant heterogeneity. For daily steps, significant subgroup differences were observed by clinical status, while intervention duration (QM = 6.09, p = 0.048) and clinical status (QM = 5.69, p = 0.017) were significant moderators. Conclusions: Chatbot interventions showed small-to-moderate post-intervention effects but limited follow-up effects. Few significant moderators were identified, underscoring the need for more rigorous RCTs.

papers.title: Four waves of cancer-related risk behaviour and personal network data from a rural Romanian community
papers.abstract: 4P-CAN is an EU-funded project that collected longitudinal personal network data to investigate how cancer-related risk behaviours are socially organised within a rural community. Respondents (egos) describe the people they know (alters), their relationships with them, and relationships among alters. We share four waves of data collected between September 2023 and September 2025 in a Romanian rural community through interviewer-assisted network interviews and link-tracing recruitment. Five linked data tables contain 353 interviews with 142 adults, 7,602 alter roster entries identifying 2,480 people, 41,354 records of ego-reported acquaintance between alters, and recruitment-node and referral records. Linking individuals across networks and waves supports investigation of how cancer-related risk behaviours are distributed and clustered across community relationships. It also supports research on network composition, overlapping networks, reported health attributes and longitudinal measurement. Reuse should account for non-probability recruitment, dependence among observations and changes in measurement across waves.

papers.title: Unboxing unhealthy food marketing: An analysis of the extent and nature of unhealthy food marketing to children on YouTube in Canada using the CHOPPED artificial intelligence system
papers.abstract: Background: Unhealthy food marketing negatively affects children's dietary patterns. However, little is known about the extent and nature of unhealthy food marketing to children on YouTube due to reliance on manual assessment methods. Objectives: To use a novel artificial intelligence (AI) system (CHild Oriented food Product Promotion Evaluation and Detection system, CHOPPED) to examine the extent and nature of unhealthy food marketing in YouTube videos suggested to Avatar accounts created for children and adults based on age and gender. Methods: Over two months of continuous monitoring, CHOPPED collected marketing instances played before, during, and after videos suggested by YouTube's algorithm to six child and two adult accounts that were not signed in and differed by age (2-4, 5-8, 9-12, =<18 years) and gender across four Canadian cities (Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, Halifax). CHOPPED characterized the extent and nature of monthly child-targeted unhealthy food marketing instances during 24-hour and typical 2-hour daily viewing periods. Results: CHOPPED collected 60,633 marketing instances. No food marketing was shown to child accounts 2-4 years. On average, child accounts (5-12 years) were shown 25 monthly unhealthy food marketing instances during a 2-hour daily viewing period, 24 of which were child-targeted. The boy's account (9-12 years) was shown a significantly higher monthly frequency of child-targeted unhealthy food marketing instances (340, 70.2%) than the boy's account (5-8 years; 241, 66.2%), the girl's account (5-8 years; 261, 60.6%), the man's account (224, 57.7%), and the woman's account (263, 54.7%) during a 24-hour (p<0.05) but not a 2-hour daily viewing period. Monthly frequencies of some core child-targeted techniques shown to the boy's account (9-12 years) were also higher than other accounts during a 24-hour (p<0.05) but not a 2-hour daily viewing period. Conclusions: This study pioneered AI-driven analysis of the extent and nature of unhealthy food marketing to children on YouTube. Children's potential exposure to such marketing on YouTube may be low. There was some evidence that the older boys' account was shown more monthly child-targeted unhealthy food marketing instances and of some core child-targeted techniques than other accounts. On YouTube, food marketing may target a general audience rather than children by age and gender.

papers.title: Cardiovascular and metabolic trajectories in men engaged in a multidimensional preventive care program: a prospective observational study
papers.abstract: ObjectivesTo describe within-individual changes in cardiometabolic, functional and neuroendocrine markers between two standardized evaluations in men engaged in a structured preventive care program, and to examine transitions across clinical risk categories. DesignProspective observational cohort study using routinely collected data; paired within-individual analyses. SettingSingle preventive health center in Paris, France, offering a standardized multidisciplinary assessment with individualized lifestyle, supplementation and, when indicated, pharmacological recommendations. Participants279 men aged 18 years or older with a first evaluation (CU1) between October 2022 and November 2025 and a second evaluation (CU2) by May 2026 (32.3% of 865 eligible men); median interval 13.3 months (IQR 12.0-15.6). No exclusion criteria were applied. Primary and secondary outcome measuresWithin-individual change in continuous markers (Hodges- Lehmann estimate, 95% CI; Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment over 36 tests) and transitions across fixed clinical thresholds (paired odds ratios). ResultsMedian age was 51.2 years, BMI 24.5 kg/m{superscript 2} and SCORE2 2.9%. Visceral adipose tissue mass decreased ({Delta} -49 g, 95% CI -80.5 to -18.5; q=0.006), with small decreases in body mass and fat mass. Handgrip strength increased (right +2.35 kg, 1.70 to 3.00; left +1.70 kg, 1.05 to 2.30; q<0.001). HDL cholesterol increased (+3.5 mg/dL, 2.5 to 4.5; q<0.001), with decreases in the triglyceride/HDL and total/HDL ratios. Blood pressure, LDL cholesterol, fasting glucose (after adjustment), insulin, HOMA-IR, SCORE2 and salivary cortisol and DHEA did not change. The proportion of men below the grip strength reference value decreased from 60.1% to 47.6% (paired OR 0.34, 0.19 to 0.61) and with HDL cholesterol [≤]46 mg/dL from 26.7% to 16.5% (OR 0.25, 0.12 to 0.54). ConclusionsIIn this selected, health-engaged population of men who completed both evaluations, changes in a favorable direction were observed for handgrip strength, HDL cholesterol and visceral adiposity, whereas blood pressure, LDL cholesterol, glycemic markers and SCORE2 were stable. Without a comparison group, these changes cannot be distinguished from regression to the mean, test-retest effects or secular trends. Strengths and limitations of this studyO_LIStandardized assessment protocol applied identically at both evaluations, combining clinical, laboratory, DEXA body composition, functional and salivary neuroendocrine measurements in the same individuals. C_LIO_LIPaired within-individual analyses of 36 markers in 279 men, reported as effect estimates with confidence intervals and a global false discovery rate adjustment, with sensitivity analyses by follow-up interval and calendar period and a comparison of returners with 586 eligible non-returners. C_LIO_LISingle-arm design without a comparison group: the observed changes cannot be distinguished from regression to the mean, test-retest effects, participation effects or secular trends. C_LIO_LIHighly selected population of urban, socioeconomically advantaged, health-engaged men, of whom 32% returned for a second evaluation, limiting generalizability to the general population and to high-risk groups. C_LIO_LIStandardized effect sizes were small for most markers, adherence to recommendations was not measured objectively, and the follow-up was short. C_LI

papers.title: Quasi-experimental evaluation of a social media campaign to promote HPV vaccination in Bauchi state, Nigeria
papers.abstract: Cervical cancer is the leading cause of cancer death in women in 26 countries, including in sub-Saharan African countries. Cervical and other cancer risks can be greatly reduced through timely HPV vaccination and early screening. But it continues to pose a significant public health challenge in LMICs such as Nigeria. This study reports on the implementation and evaluation of a pair of social media behavior change campaigns to increase HPV vaccination amongst girls ages 9-14 and reduce vaccine hesitancy amongst girls and their parents in Bauchi state, Nigeria. The primary objectives are to conduct a quasi-experimental evaluation of the social media campaign; to examine the effect of higher versus lower levels of campaign exposure on HPV vaccination and related outcomes; to determine whether the social media campaign followed its planned theory of change; and to identify which social media messages were most effective in promoting HPV vaccination. We implemented an HPV vaccination social media promotion campaign, using videos designed to encourage parents to vaccinate their daughters, at scale in Bauchi state on the Meta and TikTok social media platforms. We used a quasi-experimental design, a heavy-up approach, that experimentally manipulated the level of social media content delivered in Bauchi. We used the Virtual Lab platform, an open-source platform that uses social media to recruit participants using advertising and creates panels of respondents for data collection through an online survey, and also collected social media metrics including impressions and engagement. The campaign was effective in increasing HPV vaccination rates from 69% at baseline to 86% at endline over 2 campaign phases that spanned approximately 3 months. Based on GEE modeling, we found that higher levels of engagement with the campaign were associated with higher vaccination rates at midline and endline. Pro-vaccine attitudes and reduced vaccine hesitancy also predicted higher vaccination rates. Also, the campaign produced additional HPV vaccinations at low cost: Adjusted for campaign exposure cost of $0.81 per additional vaccination in campaign phase 1, $2.10 per vax in phase 2, and $2.40 for the total campaign period. Evidence from this study indicates that social media may be an effective strategy to promote HPV vaccination at low cost. Future rigorous trials using experimental methods are needed to further evaluate social media to promote HPV vaccination.

papers.title: Geospatial AI targeting of tuberculosis active case finding in Pune, India: a quasi-experimental evaluation
papers.abstract: BACKGROUNDActive case finding (ACF) in India screens large populations to find few cases. AI-NETRA predicts neighbourhood-level tuberculosis (TB) risk from routine notification data and generates field microplans. OBJECTIVETo compare the yield and efficiency of AI-guided and standard ACF, and frontline acceptability. DESIGNProspective quasi-experimental evaluation in four TB Units of Pune district, comparing two-week AI-guided sweeps (April to May 2026) with the routine campaign in the same units (December 2024 to January 2025). Primary endpoint: bacteriologically confirmed pulmonary TB per persons screened; secondary: all-forms yield, presumptive yield, referral precision, number needed to screen (NNS) and cost per case. Acceptability: 16 focus groups (n=100) and a survey of 101 ASHAs. RESULTSAI-guided teams screened 66,095 people and confirmed 10 pulmonary cases, against 9 among 177,322 in the standard campaign (rate ratio 2.98, 95% CI 1.09 to 8.29); NNS was 6,610 versus 19,702 and cost per case 66% lower. All-forms detection did not differ (15 versus 32; RR 1.26, 95% CI 0.63 to 2.39); the standard campaign had mobile X-ray. 96% of ASHAs reported finding the same presumptive cases while screening fewer people. CONCLUSIONGeospatial targeting raised confirmed yield per person and lowered NNS; total detection did not differ. A concurrent, like-for-like trial is warranted.

papers.title: DEVELOPMENT AND INTERNAL EVALUATION OF MODELS FOR PREDICTING PROLONGED HOSPITALISATION AMONG PATIENTS WITH SICKLE CELL DISEASE IN A PUBLIC UNIVERSITY HOSPITAL IN GHANA
papers.abstract: BackgroundProlonged hospitalisation is an important burden among patients with sickle cell disease (SCD), with implications for healthcare utilisation and patient and caregiver burden. Early prediction may support timely clinical and resource-management interventions. ObjectiveTo identify factors associated with prolonged hospitalisation among patients with SCD and compare the predictive performance of multivariable logistic regression with five supervised machine-learning algorithms. MethodsThis retrospective study included SCD inpatients aged [≥]16 years admitted to the University of Ghana Hospital between January 2019 and December 2024. Logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, support vector machine, and k-nearest neighbours models were developed using five-fold stratified cross-validation. Class weighting and SMOTE were applied within training folds. Model performance was evaluated using AUC-ROC, AUC-PR, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), F1 score, and balanced accuracy. ResultsAmong 872 patients, 137 (15.7%) experienced prolonged hospitalisation. Acute chest syndrome (aOR=4.28; 95% CI: 2.31-7.94), malaria (aOR=3.77; 95% CI: 2.11-6.74), pneumonia (aOR=3.45; 95% CI: 2.02-5.90), and anaemia (aOR=2.71; 95% CI: 1.13-6.51) were independently associated with prolonged hospitalisation, whereas higher haemoglobin was protective (aOR=0.86; 95% CI: 0.78-0.96). Logistic regression achieved the highest AUC-ROC (0.692), F1 score (0.418) and balanced accuracy (0.677), while random forest achieved the highest AUC-PR (0.375). KNN had the highest sensitivity (59.3%) and XGBoost the highest specificity (87.2%). AUC-ROC confidence intervals overlapped substantially across models. ConclusionInfection-related complications and anaemia were important predictors of prolonged hospitalisation, while higher haemoglobin was protective. ML models showed modest performance without clear superiority over logistic regression. Larger multicentre studies with external validation are warranted.

papers.title: Antibiotic receipt by respiratory symptom group and source of care among children under five in Bangladesh: repeated cross-sectional analyses of national surveys, 2019 and 2025
papers.abstract: BackgroundAntibiotic use for childhood respiratory illness is common in low-income and middle-income countries, but national surveys rarely separate symptom groups or care pathways. We estimated antibiotic receipt among children under five in Bangladesh by reported respiratory symptom group, source of care and household wealth. MethodsWe analysed the 2019 and 2025 Bangladesh Multiple Indicator Cluster Surveys. We included 4,010 children with cough and difficult breathing in the previous two weeks (3,990 in regression models). We compared breathing difficulty from the chest (suspected pneumonia) with nose-only symptoms, and five reported sources of care. Survey-weighted modified Poisson regression estimated adjusted prevalence ratios (PRs). We described where antibiotic-treated children sought care and estimated slope indices of inequality (SIIs) by wealth. ResultsIn 2025, 68.5% (95% CI 64.2 to 72.5) of children with suspected pneumonia received an antibiotic, as did 54.3% (51.3 to 57.2) of children with nose-only symptoms. In pooled analyses of both surveys, the adjusted PR for nose-only symptoms was 0.83 (0.78 to 0.89). Against public health care, the pooled adjusted PR was 0.98 (0.91 to 1.07) for pharmacy care without a medical facility. It was 0.24 (0.20 to 0.29) for no advice or treatment sought. Pharmacy care rose from 18.8% to 36.5% of children with cough and difficult breathing between 2019 and 2025. By 2025, it accounted for 43.7% of treated children with suspected pneumonia and 42.2% with nose-only symptoms. Across the pooled surveys, receipt for suspected pneumonia was higher in richer children (SII 12.5 percentage points, 1.0 to 24.0). Recorded amoxicillin receipt in suspected pneumonia was 17.7% (14.7 to 21.1) in 2025, with no clear wealth gradient. ConclusionsAntibiotic receipt was common in both symptom groups, and care contacts shifted towards pharmacies. Receipt and care seeking differed by wealth. Antibiotic receipt should be monitored alongside symptoms and care contacts. Stewardship should be evaluated in medical and pharmacy settings while protecting access to assessment and appropriate treatment. The surveys cannot determine whether individual courses were appropriate.

papers.title: Evaluating menstrual-friendly public bathrooms in Atlanta, Georgia: An audit of availability, accessibility, and resources
papers.abstract: Public toilets are essential urban infrastructure that enable people who menstruate to participate in public life with dignity and comfort. However, little is known about whether publicly accessible toilets adequately support menstrual health and hygiene, particularly in high-income urban settings where privately operated facilities often function as de facto public infrastructure. This study assessed the menstrual friendliness of publicly accessible toilets in Atlanta, Georgia. We also examined differences by funding source (i.e., government versus private) and neighborhood type. We conducted field-based audits of womens, gender-neutral, and family toilets across 15 areas. Using an adapted Menstrual Friendly Public Toilet framework, we evaluated six dimensions: cleanliness, privacy and safety, structural features, general resources, accessibility, and menstrual health and hygiene resources. We calculated domain-specific and overall scores and compared government- and privately funded facilities, with additional descriptive comparisons across business, residential, tourist, and transit neighborhoods. We audited 125 toilet facilities across 112 locations. The overall mean Menstrual Friendly Public Toilet Index was 0.797. Cleanliness (0.974), privacy and safety (0.954), structure (0.930), and general resources (0.899) scored relatively high, whereas accessibility (0.622) and menstrual health and hygiene resources (0.490) scored lowest. Only 4.0% of facilities provided menstrual products or a functional dispenser. Overall scores did not differ significantly by funding source, although government-funded facilities had higher structural feature scores than privately funded facilities (0.952 versus 0.913; p=0.027). Menstrual health and hygiene resource scores varied across neighborhood types, ranging from 0.200 in the residential area to 0.775 in the tourist area. These findings demonstrate that the availability of clean and functional bathrooms does not necessarily ensure people can fully meet and manage their menstrual needs. Addressing gaps in accessibility and menstrual-specific resources will require coordinated attention to both government- and privately managed facilities, as well as consideration of neighborhood context to support menstrual health and equitable participation in urban public spaces.

papers.title: Projecting Introduction Timelines for Cholera Conjugate Vaccine and Typhoid-Cholera Conjugate Combo Vaccine: A Scenario-Based Forecasting Approach
papers.abstract: ObjectiveThis study aimed to project introduction timing and pathways of cholera conjugate vaccine (CCV) and combined typhoid-cholera conjugate vaccines (TCV/CCVs) in 39 low- and middle-income countries and to assess potential barriers to their routine immunization integration. MethodsAccelerated failure time models were fitted using oral cholera vaccine (OCV) introduction as a proxy for CCV adoption. Country-level estimates were standardized using observed post-WHO-prequalification introduction intervals for analogous vaccine transitions. TCV/CCV introduction timing and pathways were projected by combining standardized CCV estimates with a TCV introduction priority index based on typhoid burden and previous vaccination experience. Potential barriers to routine immunization integration were assessed using semi-quantitative scoring approach. ResultsGavi, the Vaccine Alliance (Gavi) eligibility, greater previous OCV experience, and higher cholera intensity were associated with earlier introduction times. After standardization, the median projected time to CCV introduction was 6.9 years after WHO prequalification, with 12 countries introducing within five years. The TCV/CCV projections comprised three pathways: CCV introduction followed by transition to TCV/CCV, direct TCV/CCV introduction and continued CCV use without TCV/CCV introduction during the analysis period. Projected introduction timing was not consistently aligned with routine integration barrier levels for either vaccine. ConclusionsThese scenario-based projections provide an early indication of where and when demand may emerge and which countries may require additional programmatic or financing support. The findings can inform demand forecasting, market assessment, manufacturing and supply planning, investment decisions, and introduction preparedness, but the projections should be recalibrated as product-specific evidence becomes available.

papers.title: Generative AI Versus Primary Care Physicians from Plan Initiation to Long-Term Maintenance of Chronic Disease Self-Management: A Vignette-Based Validation Study
papers.abstract: BackgroundGenerative artificial intelligence (GenAI) may provide personalised and dynamically adjustable support for chronic disease self-management. However, previous studies have largely focused on isolated questions and a limited range of evaluation dimensions. ObjectiveTo compare the quality of self-management advice generated by GenAI and primary care physicians (PCPs) across multiple stages of chronic disease management and evaluation dimensions. MethodsWe conducted a cross-sectional, source-blinded comparative evaluation using 15 standardised vignettes of diabetes and hypertension derived from authentic primary care follow-up records. Each vignette comprised three sequential management stages, with medical accuracy, readability, and behaviour-change potential assessed across the three simulated stages; individualisation and multidisciplinary integration at plan initiation; contextual adaptability during acute adjustment; and empathy during long-term maintenance. The GenAI system and 22 PCPs independently generated advice which was independently rated by three clinicians, one each from general practice, endocrinology, and cardiology. across seven dimensions. Linear mixed-effects models were used for the primary comparisons, and case-level paired and physician-distribution analyses were conducted as robustness analyses. ResultsThe GenAI system achieved estimated marginal means above 4.0 in all dimensions except readability. It scored significantly higher than PCPs in six of the seven dimensions, with adjusted mean differences ranging from 1.16 to 1.56 points (P<.001). Readability was the only exception, with no significant difference between GenAI and PCPs (-0.22, 95% CI -0.54 to 0.11; P=.19). The GenAI mean exceeded the individual means of all recruited PCPs in the six dimensions but ranked at approximately the 23rd percentile for readability. ConclusionsOur findings indicated the GenAI system may generate more highly rated self-management advice than PCPs across most evaluated dimensions but offered no advantage in readability. These findings provide pre-implementation evidence for GenAI as a potential source of structured and adaptive chronic disease self-management support. Patient-level pilot studies and subsequent randomised trials are needed to determine its acceptability and effects on behaviour and clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Determinants of mpox vaccine acceptance among peri-urban residents in Sekondi-Takoradi, Western Region of Ghana: A community-based cross-sectional study
papers.abstract: Mpox re-emerged as a global public health concern in 2022, and the Western Region of Ghana became the epicentre of the countrys largest recorded outbreak in 2025. Ahead of a sub-national vaccination campaign launched in October 2025, no study had examined the determinants of mpox vaccine acceptance among peri-urban residents of the region using a theoretically grounded framework. This study determined the sociodemographic and Health Belief Model-based determinants of mpox vaccine acceptance among peri-urban residents of the Sekondi-Takoradi Metropolis, Western Region, Ghana. A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 580 adults in six purposively selected peri-urban areas and their surrounding communities between July and August 2025, before the vaccination campaign began. Vaccine acceptance was measured as a three-category outcome (accept, hesitant, refuse) and analysed using chi-square tests and multinomial logistic regression adjusted for sociodemographic characteristics, Health Belief Model constructs, and peri-urban area. Overall, 75.7% of respondents were willing to accept the vaccine, 12.9% were hesitant and 11.4% would refuse. Perceived vaccine safety was the strongest determinant: respondents who considered the vaccine very safe had markedly lower adjusted odds of hesitancy (adjusted odds ratio 0.02, 95% confidence interval 0.00-0.12) and refusal (0.03, 0.01-0.13) than those who considered it unsafe. Uncertainty about vaccine effectiveness was associated with hesitancy (9.83, 1.95-49.50), and belief in its effectiveness with lower odds of refusal (0.22, 0.06-0.86). Higher educational attainment was associated with lower odds of hesitancy, being a student or employed with lower odds of refusal, and acceptance differed between peri-urban areas (55.1% to 95.6%). Knowledge of mpox transmission was associated with acceptance in bivariate analysis (p < 0.001) but not after adjustment. Risk communication that addresses vaccine safety and effectiveness, rather than generic disease-awareness messaging alone, is likely to be most effective in improving mpox vaccine acceptance in this population, with unemployed and less-educated residents warranting targeting. As a pre-campaign baseline collected during an active outbreak, these findings can inform the vaccination response in the Western Region and preparedness in comparable peri-urban West African settings.

papers.title: Determinants of early child development among children aged 24-59 months in Ethiopia: 2024-25 Demographic and Health Survey
papers.abstract: BackgroundThe 2024-25 Ethiopia Demographic and Health Survey (EDHS) is the first national survey in Ethiopia to measure early childhood development using UNICEFs Early Childhood Development Index 2030 (ECDI2030). This provides a national estimate for Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) indicator 4.2.1, the proportion of children aged 24-59 months who are developmentally on track. We estimated the prevalence of being developmentally on track and examined its child, maternal, household and community determinants in Ethiopia. MethodsThis cross-sectional study analysed 3,731 children aged 24-59 months (weighted n = 3,514) of 3,232 mothers in 771 clusters. Children were on track if they achieved the age-specific minimum number of the 20 ECDI2030 milestones. Prevalence was estimated with design-based methods. Four three-level mixed-effects logistic regression models (children within mothers within clusters) were fitted, and interviewer effects were assessed. ResultsOverall, 36.3% (95% CI 33.4-39.3) of children were developmentally on track. Prevalence ranged from 23.3% in Southwest Regional State, Ethiopia, to 77.7% in Addis Ababa. In the null model, 21.5% of the variation lay between clusters (median odds ratio 3.24). In the final model, the odds of being on track were lower at 36-47 months (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] 0.57, 95% CI 0.44-0.74) and 48-59 months (AOR 0.39, 0.30-0.51) than at 24-35 months. They were also lower after a preceding birth interval under 24 months (AOR 0.75, 0.57-0.99), after recent diarrhoea, fever or cough (AOR 0.59, 0.45-0.77), and where distance to a health facility was a big problem (AOR 0.61, 0.48-0.79). Odds were higher for girls (AOR 1.38, 1.12-1.70), with maternal education (more than secondary vs none: AOR 2.08, 1.19-3.63) and with weekly media exposure (AOR 2.15, 1.51-3.06). The covariates explained 55.9% of the between-cluster variance. ConclusionsNearly two in three Ethiopian children aged 24-59 months are not developmentally on track, and children fall further behind as they age. Interventions should target maternal education, access to information and health services, birth spacing and childhood illness, with priority for the lowest-performing regions and communities.

papers.title: Gender Differences in Socioeconomic Inequalities in Body Mass Index and Health-Related Mediators Among Young and Early Midlife Finns
papers.abstract: IntroductionSocioeconomic differences in body mass index (BMI) are well established, but less is known about gender differences and their behavioral pathways. We examined gender differences in the association between socioeconomic position (SEP) and BMI, and whether dietary factors and physical activity mediated the associations. MethodsWe used survey data from the employees of the City of Helsinki aged 19-39 collected in 2017 (n = 4,400, 80% women). SEP was measured by highest educational attainment, and the examined mediators were consumption of fruit and vegetables, red and processed meat, sweets and confectionery and alcohol as well as leisure-time vigorous physical activity (VPA) and sedentary time. We conducted gender-specific multiple mediation analyses using structural equation modeling and additional analyses using multiple imputation by chained equations. ResultsWith increasing educational attainment, mean BMI decreased from 26.4 kg/m{superscript 2} to 24.0 kg/m{superscript 2} among women, and from 26.6 kg/m{superscript 2} to 25.2 kg/m{superscript 2} among men. Lower SEP was associated with lower consumption of fruit and vegetables, higher consumption of red and processed meat, and lower VPA in both genders. Women reported healthier diets but less VPA than men. The strongest SEP-BMI mediator among women was VPA (indirect effect: 0.35, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.26, 0.44), followed by fruit and vegetable consumption (0.15, 95% CI 0.08, 0.23) and red and processed meat consumption (0.06, 95% CI 0.02, 0.11). Among men, significant mediators were red and processed meat consumption (0.12, 95% CI 0.03, 0.23), sedentary time (0.11, 95% CI 0.01, 0.24) and VPA (0.10, 95% CI 0.02, 0.21). ConclusionsSocioeconomic inequalities in BMI appear stronger among women and are shaped through partly different mechanisms between genders. Improving VPA may be relevant among low- SEP women, whereas reducing sedentary time may be more relevant among low-SEP men. Reducing red and processed meat is beneficial for both genders.

papers.title: Functional difficulty among children and adolescents aged 5-17 years in Ethiopia: Multilevel analysis of the nationally representative 2024-2025 DHS
papers.abstract: BackgroundPopulation-based data on functional difficulty among school-age children in Ethiopia are scarce. The 2024-2025 Ethiopia Demographic and Health Survey (EDHS) included, for the first time, the UNICEF/Washington Group Child Functioning Module (CFM) for children aged 5-17 years. We estimated the prevalence and domain distribution of functional difficulty and associated factors in Ethiopia. MethodsWe analysed cross-sectional EDHS data from 11,122 children aged 5-17 years (weighted n = 10,726) and 4,739 mothers. Functional difficulty was defined as "a lot of difficulty" or "cannot do at all" in any of 11 domains, or daily anxiety or depression. We estimated design-based prevalence and fitted multilevel logistic regression models (children within mothers within clusters) for any, non-affective and affective difficulty. Interviewer effects were examined with random-intercept models and within-cluster comparisons. ResultsOverall, 9.5% (95% CI 8.1-11.1) of children had functional difficulty. Daily depression (6.8%) and anxiety (6.6%) dominated, and 70.3% of affected children had only affective difficulty. Difficulty in at least one non-affective domain affected 2.8% (2.2-3.7), with each domain at 0.5-1.4%. Prevalence ranged from 1.5% in Southwest Regional State, Ethiopia, to 16.5% in Oromia Regional State. In adjusted models, children not attending school had higher odds of non-affective difficulty (AOR 2.82, 95% CI 2.01-3.96), and girls had lower odds (AOR 0.63, 0.48-0.84). Outcomes clustered strongly within families (sibling correlation 67.7%) and clusters (ICC 20.9%). Six of 163 interviewers (7.9% of the weighted sample) contributed 58.2% of weighted cases of daily anxiety or depression; in the same clusters they recorded daily symptoms for 56.4% of children, against 2.1% for other interviewers. Excluding 11 statistically outlying interviewers reduced the prevalence of any difficulty to 4.6% (3.6-5.8) and of daily anxiety or depression to 3.3%. The associations with school non-attendance and sex were unchanged. ConclusionsFunctional difficulties across the sensory, physical, cognitive, and affective domains, including anxiety or depression, affect about 2-3% of Ethiopian children aged 5-17 years and are strongly associated with being out of school. Appropriate interventions and resource allocation should be considered.

papers.title: The Evolving Role of Telehealth in Routine Health Care Delivery Among US Adults, 2022-2024
papers.abstract: BackgroundTelehealth use expanded rapidly during the COVID-19 pandemic, but its role following the end of the public health emergency (PHE) remains incompletely understood. This study examined changes in telehealth utilization among US adults between 2022 and 2024, characteristics associated with use, and changes in self-reported reasons for using telehealth to understand its evolving role. MethodsThis serial cross-sectional study analyzed nationally representative data from 13 141 US adults participating in the Health Information National Trends Survey (HINTS) in 2022, during the COVID-19 PHE, and 2024, after the PHE ended. Survey-weighted analyses were used to estimate telehealth utilization and self-reported reasons for use. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression was used to examine changes between survey cycles and sociodemographic and health-related characteristics associated with telehealth utilization. Multiple imputation was used to address missing data. ResultsTelehealth utilization declined from 39.3% in 2022 to 34.5% in 2024; after adjustment for sociodemographic and health-related characteristics, the odds of telehealth use were significantly lower in 2024 than in 2022 (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.81; 95% CI, 0.69-0.95). Telehealth utilization differed across population groups. Higher odds of use were observed among adults aged 35 to 49 years (aOR, 1.47; 95% CI, 1.19-1.82), those with a college degree or higher (aOR, 1.93; 95% CI, 1.31-2.86), those with diagnosed depression or anxiety (aOR, 2.86; 95% CI, 2.46-3.33), those with a history of cancer (aOR, 1.40; 95% CI, 1.15-1.69), and insured adults (aOR, 1.52; 95% CI, 1.13-2.04). All self-reported reasons for telehealth use declined between 2022 and 2024. Infection avoidance decreased from 50.2% to 19.1% and provider recommendation or requirement from 72.8% to 47.2%, whereas convenience showed a smaller decline from 65.6% to 56.2% and became the leading reported reason for telehealth use in 2024. ConclusionsTelehealth utilization declined between 2022 and 2024, while the relative persistence of convenience as a reason for use suggests a shift away from pandemic-driven demand toward more selective integration into routine health care. Differences in utilization across population groups suggest that telehealth may address some barriers to conventional care while access remains uneven. These findings highlight the evolving role of telehealth after the COVID-19 PHE and the importance of supporting its appropriate and equitable integration into routine care.

papers.title: Measuring community building in group antenatal care: Evidence from a randomized trial in Malawi
papers.abstract: Improving the quality of antenatal care is essential for reducing persistently high maternal and neonatal mortality in Malawi. Group antenatal care has demonstrated improvements in quality, satisfaction, health behaviors, and outcomes. However, the impact of community building, one of the models core components, has not previously been quantitatively assessed. This study examined the measurement properties of two community building measures, assessed the impact of group antenatal care on these measures, and explored their potential role as mediators of health outcomes. This secondary analysis used quantitative data from the parent study testing the effectiveness of group antenatal care at seven clinics in Blantyre District, Malawi. The Perinatal Peer Support Scale and the Provider Connectedness subscale of the Pregnancy Related Empowerment Scale were used to measure community building and were validated using factor analyses. Results supported a two-factor structure for perinatal peer support (relational support and peer network) and a unidimensional structure for provider connectedness. Using generalized linear modeling, we found that participation in group antenatal care was associated with significantly stronger community building across all measures when compared to usual individual antenatal care. Women in group antenatal care demonstrated higher relational support score, peer network, and provider connectedness scores compared with women in individual antenatal care (p < 0.001). However, we found no evidence that community building had direct or indirect (mediating) effects on maternal psychological distress or infant birthweight. This study strengthens the evidence base for group antenatal care by validating measures of community building and showing that relational support, peer networks, and provider connectedness are important benefits of participation. Although community building did not mediate the outcomes examined here, the findings highlight the need to further test of theoretical pathways linking group antenatal care to maternal and child health outcomes.

papers.title: Age-related Trust and its Association with Cost-related Medication Nonadherence
papers.abstract: Trust operates foundationally at the personal and societal levels, a vital force that drives social connection, cooperation, and positive outcomes. In healthcare, trust is instrumental in improving patient outcomes as it forms the foundation for shared decision-making and patient-provider relationships. With growing evidence that generalized trust toward other people grows with age and behaviors such as cost-related medication non-adherence (CRN) decrease with age we study whether lack of trust is a force that drives up CRN and its variability in effects across age groups, controlling for other risk factors. The data consists of 680 Medicare diabetes patients at high risk of hospitalization enrolled in a randomized controlled trial of the effect of the Comprehensive Care Physician model (CCP) at an academic medical center between November 2012 and June 2016. This study provides first-of-its-kind evidence that lack of trust is an important force that drives up CRN and the effect of lack of trust decreased even though the lack of trust decreased by age increments. The effect of lack of trust is particularly pronounced among younger patients. For practice and policy, it shows the potential promising prospect that a more trusting attitude may be conducive to more productive health. More research is needed on how to build trust at the societal level and in healthcare specifically, and how generalized trust and target-specific trust of providers are correlated.

papers.title: Displaced by a Volcano: Adolescent Well-Being in Uncertain Times in Iceland 2023-2026
papers.abstract: AimsThe November 2023 evacuation of Grindavik, Iceland, left families facing prolonged uncertainty about return. We examined adolescent well-being before and after evacuation and changes in gaps with national peers between 2025 and 2026. MethodsRepeated cross-sectional analyses used the 2023, 2025, and 2026 Icelandic Youth Study waves, adjusting for grade, gender, and non-Icelandic background. The towns single school in 2023 provided the pre-evacuation benchmark, with models accounting for national time trends. Adolescents who moved before evacuation provided a mobility benchmark. ResultsIn 2025, evacuees reported lower life satisfaction and school belonging, more psychosomatic symptoms, and higher odds of school absence and past-30-day substance use than the national reference group. The three well-being outcomes departed from the pre-evacuation pattern. Life-satisfaction and belonging gaps were larger among girls than boys in 2025, but these gender differences narrowed by 2026. Comparisons with prior movers suggested a distinct evacuation-related pattern in 2025 among evacuee girls, who reported lower life satisfaction and school belonging than prior-mover girls. In 2026, psychosomatic symptoms (B = 0.29, 95% CI [0.08, 0.49]), absenteeism (OR = 1.81, 95% CI [1.26, 2.60]), and substance use (OR = 2.59, 95% CI [1.75, 3.84]) remained higher relative to the national reference group. Life satisfaction and belonging were directionally lower, with intervals including zero. Change estimates did not establish narrowing of the gaps. ConclusionsThe findings underscore the need for sustained educational and well-being support to address adolescents social connections alongside their mental health during prolonged displacement, including in a Nordic welfare setting.

papers.title: PNEUMOCOCCAL CONJUGATE VACCINE SCHEDULES SHAPE SEROTYPE-SPECIFIC MEMORY B-CELL RESPONSES
papers.abstract: Reduced-dose pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV) schedules ( 1+1; one primary and one booster) are now endorsed by the World Health Organisation under specific circumstances. Serotype-specific memory B cells (BMEM) are a marker of long-term protection but data from infant reduced-dose trials remain limited. As part of a randomised controlled trial in Vietnamese infants, we characterised serotype-specific BMEM responses in randomised subsets (N=50 per vaccine group per timepoint) following 0+1 (at 12 months of age) or 1+1 (2 and 12 months of age) schedules of PCV10 or PCV13, using a multimer spectral flow cytometry approach. Blood samples were collected at 12 months of age (baseline) and at day 7 and day 28 post-vaccination. A one or two dose schedule of either PCV induced robust serotype-specific BMEM responses at day 7 and day 28 for most serotypes. PCV13 generated earlier and higher BMEM responses than PCV10, while 1+1 schedules for either PCV produced higher BMEM responses than the 0+1 schedules at day 7. By day 28, these differences between the 0+1 and 1+1 schedules were no longer apparent. Notably, BMEM responses for serotypes 6B and 23F were detectable even in infants who did not achieve protective levels of serotype-specific IgG [≥]0.35 {micro}g/mL. PCV13 generated higher plasmablast and plasma cell responses by day 7, and higher cTfh responses by day 28, compared to PCV10. These findings show that 1+1 schedules of PCV10 or PCV13 induce robust BMEM responses, with important implications for the evaluation of PCVs and understanding long-term protection.

papers.title: Implementing community-based minimally invasive tissue sampling for mortality surveillance in rural South Africa: A process evaluation of the Vukamberi project
papers.abstract: Accurate cause-of-death data are limited in rural low- and middle-income settings, where most deaths occur at home without medical certification. Minimally invasive tissue sampling (MITS) is a culturally acceptable alternative to complete autopsy but has largely been applied to stillbirths and child deaths. We evaluated the process and implementation of a community-based, all-age MITS study in rural South Africa. The Vukamberi project ("to examine" in Xitsonga) is a prospective study in rural Bushbuckridge sub-district, Mpumalanga Province. Guided by the Medical Research Council Framework for Complex Interventions and Proctors Implementation Outcomes Framework, we assessed reach, adoption, fidelity, feasibility, acceptability and timeliness using prospectively collected records of deaths notified between 07 July 2024 to 30 June 2026, and mapped challenges to adaptive strategies by domain and phase. All 408 notified community deaths were screened, and 316 (77.5%) were eligible. Families consented for 206 eligible cases (65.2%), all of which proceeded to MITS, with target-organ sampling adherence in 199 (96.6%). Median time from death to notification was 15 hours (interquartile range [IQR] 5-23) and to MITS completion 37 hours (IQR 25-49). Enrolled decedents were 197 adults (95.6%) and 9 paediatric cases (4.4%). Main ineligibility reasons were in-hospital death (excluded by design; 27 cases) and notification beyond 48 hours (26 cases). Family refusal, mostly reflecting grief-related unreadiness and sociocultural barriers, accounted for 53 (48.2%) non-enrolled eligible cases. Adaptive strategies that increased enrolment included extending recruitment beyond the Agincourt Health and Socio- Demographic Surveillance System into the wider sub-district, incentivised community informants, elder-mediated consent, gender-appropriate field staff, non-disfigurement messaging in local languages and mortuary-based consenting where household access was restricted by a traditional leader. Community-based MITS was feasible in this rural setting. Culturally responsive consent strategies, mortuary partnerships and multi-channel death notification helped overcome sociocultural and logistical barriers, and a reliable supply of consumables proved essential for continuous enrolment. These findings may inform community-based mortality surveillance in other low- and middle-income settings.

papers.title: Wealth inequalities malaria parasitaemia and child anaemia in Nigeria
papers.abstract: Anaemia and malaria remain concentrated among children living in poorer households in Nigeria, but the extent to which the wealth gradient in anaemia operates through current malaria parasitaemia is uncertain. We used three nationally representative surveys to estimate a clearly defined parasitaemia-mediated component of the association, while recognising that anaemia has multiple infectious, nutritional, genetic, and social causes. We analysed de facto children aged 6-59 months in the 2010, 2015, and 2021 Nigeria Malaria Indicator Surveys. Within each survey, we contrasted children in the poorest quintile with children in the richer and richest quintiles. The outcome was altitude-adjusted anaemia and the mediator was microscopy-confirmed parasitaemia. Weighted outcome and mediator models adjusted for child age and sex, maternal education, urban residence, geopolitical zone, household size, rainy-season interview, and altitude. We standardized interventional total, direct, and indirect effects using g- computation. Missing data were addressed with 20 chained-equation imputations; uncertainty used 1,000 Rao-Wu survey-bootstrap replicates. Analytic samples included 3,307, 3,643, and 6,572 children in 2010, 2015, and 2021. The multiple-imputation total risk difference was 11.0 (95% CI 4.1 to 17.9) percentage points in 2015 and 12.5 (95% CI 8.4 to 16.6) points in 2021; corresponding parasitaemia-mediated indirect differences were 3.4 (95% CI 1.4 to 5.4) and 2.0 (95% CI 1.1 to 2.9) points. The 2010 total-effect interval included zero. Proportion-mediated estimates were withheld for 2010 and 2015 because of unstable total- effect denominators. The poorest-to-richer/richest contrast was associated with higher anaemia risk in 2015 and 2021. A smaller positive component was compatible with mediation through microscopy-confirmed parasitaemia. Because wealth, parasitaemia, and haemoglobin were measured in the same survey visit, the estimates require assumptions about temporal ordering and unmeasured mediator-outcome confounding; they do not establish that eliminating parasitaemia would remove the observed anaemia inequality.

papers.title: Disease-Specific Trends and Ethnic Inequities in In-Hospital Cardiovascular Mortality in Suriname, 2013-2022
papers.abstract: ObjectiveTo examine temporal trends in in-hospital mortality among patients hospitalized with heart failure, ischemic heart disease, and cerebrovascular disease in Suriname from 2013 to 2022, and to assess differences according to age, sex, and ethnicity. MethodsConducted a retrospective hospital-based observational study using routinely collected discharge data from three major public hospitals in Suriname. These hospitals accounted for approximately 71.8% of national hospital admissions. Admissions with a primary diagnosis of HF (ICD-10 I50), IHD (I20-I25), or Stroke (I60-I69) were included. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Separate multivariable logistic regression models were fitted for each disease, adjusting for calendar year, age, sex, and ethnicity. ResultsAmong 84,691 admissions, 42,301 were IHD, 24,584 for Stroke, and 17,806 for HF. In-hospital mortality declined significantly across all three conditions, with adjusted odds decreasing by 14% annually for HF (aOR 0.858; 95% CI 0.841-0.875), 6% for IHD (aOR 0.941; 95% CI 0.914-0.969), and 5% for Stroke (aOR 0.947; 95% CI 0.931-0.963). Increasing age was associated with higher mortality in IHD and Stroke. Female sex was associated with lower mortality in HF (aOR 0.835; 95% CI 0.744-0.937). Ethnic disparities were most pronounced for Stroke, with higher mortality among Maroon, Creole, Javanese, and Other groups than Hindustani patients. ConclusionsIn-hospital mortality declined across cardiovascular conditions, but improvements were heterogeneous. Pronounced ethnic inequalities in Stroke mortality and age-related gradients highlight the need for equity-focused cardiovascular surveillance and provide a baseline for evaluating future health-system and prevention initiatives in Suriname.

papers.title: Intersectional Inequalities in Mental Health Need and Youth Justice Contact among Pupils enrolled in Alternative Provision
papers.abstract: BackgroundUnmet mental health and education needs increase the risk of youth justice contact. Understanding inequalities in alternative provision (AP) and how these relate to school recorded mental health needs or police criminalisation may identify opportunities to intervene. MethodsWe analysed population-level linked school and police administrative data for 3.7m pupils (born 1997-2003) who attended state schools in England. We examined differences by racial-ethnic group and gender in rates and timing of AP enrolment and recording patterns of mental health-related provision and youth justice contacts among pupils with AP enrolment. ResultsOur findings indicate heightened mental health need and vulnerability to criminalisation among pupils recorded with AP enrolment. Enrolment was highest among Irish Traveller and Romani pupils, followed by Black Caribbean and Mixed White-Black Caribbean pupils. Boys were enrolled more than girls, but some girls had higher rates than boys from other groups. Over 50% boys from Black Caribbean and Mixed White-Black Caribbean backgrounds with AP enrolment had a youth justice contact, the majority of whom had recorded mental health needs. ConclusionHeightened need and intersectional inequalities among pupils enrolled in AP highlight the importance of a co-ordinated public health approach to understanding and responding to childrens needs.

papers.title: Impact of transnational gentrification on the health of adults from the EPIPorto cohort: a quasi-experimental study
papers.abstract: Gentrification is a global, accelerating urban process involving complex socio-spatial transformations. Although increasingly recognised as a determinant of urban health, quantitative evidence on its population health impacts remains scarce and inconsistent, limiting evidence-informed urban policymaking, especially in rapidly gentrifying contexts. Thus, we assessed the health impact of neighbourhood-level gentrification among adults in Porto (Northern Portugal), a hotspot of transnational gentrification. A quasi-experimental study was conducted using data from the EPIPorto population-based cohort (1999-2022), with 2,485 participants at baseline. A validated, context-sensitive 16-variable index of transnational gentrification, derived from 2011 and 2021 census and tourism-accommodation data through Principal Component Analysis, enabled neighbourhood classification as gentrifying or non-gentrifying. Difference-in-differences models estimated the effect of living in gentrifying neighbourhoods on ten cardiometabolic and behavioural outcomes. Inverse probability of censoring weighting was used to account for loss to follow-up and missing data. At baseline, 26.2% of participants resided in gentrifying neighbourhoods. Residence in a gentrifying neighbourhood was associated with a statistically significant reduction in nightly sleep duration (-0.346 h; 95% CI -0.650, -0.042), with statistically significant reductions in the lower-education and [≥]65-year subgroups. No significant effects were observed for body mass index, overweight/obesity, total/HDL/LDL cholesterol, blood pressure, and tobacco or alcohol use. Transnational gentrification in Porto showed limited effects on most cardiometabolic outcomes but was associated with reduced sleep duration, suggesting that the health impacts of gentrification may initially emerge through psychosocial pathways before translating into measurable cardiometabolic changes.

papers.title: Adapting a Shared Digital Communication Intervention for Caregivers of Children with Physical Disabilities and Professionals through Co-design: A Workshop Study
papers.abstract: IntroductionCaregivers of children with disabilities act as intermediaries between professionals due to fragmented communication and information sharing across sectors. The use of shared digital communication may support integrated care. Therefore, this study explored challenges and needs among caregivers and professionals and how an existing shared digital communication intervention could be adapted to support communication and coordination in this context. MethodsThree future workshops involved 26 co-designers: caregivers (n=8), professionals across sectors (n=14), and software developers (n=4). Caregiver and professional data were analysed thematically, followed by matrix analysis to identify convergences, tensions, and design principles. In workshop with software developers, design principles were translated into design specifications. ResultsBoth caregivers and professionals described how caregivers become de facto care coordinators. Clear responsibilities, continuity, and shared knowledge were identified as essential for improving communication and coordination. Shared digital communication was considered promising, but tensions emerged between accessibility and workload, and between transparency and confidentiality. The adapted intervention incorporated structured communication, shared responsibility, relational continuity, a shared overview, and a human digital coordination function. Discussion/conclusionThe adapted intervention provides a foundation for cross-sector communication between caregivers and professionals and adds to the evidence base of communication solutions that may strengthen integrated care.

papers.title: Mental Health-related School Provision and Hospital Contacts among Pupils enrolled in Alternative Provision
papers.abstract: BackgroundPupils enrolled in Alternative Provision (AP) represent a highly vulnerable population, with heightened mental health need at risk of long-term educational disengagement. Examining AP enrolment in relation to mental health-related school support and hospital contacts may inform early intervention and prevention approaches to address unmet mental health need. MethodsWe analysed population-level linked school and hospital administrative data for 1.7m pupils (born 2000-2002) who attended state schools in England. We examined differences by racial-ethnic group and gender in rates and timing of AP enrolment and recording patterns of mental health-related provision and hospital contacts among pupils with AP enrolment. ResultsA majority (62.4%) of pupils with AP enrolment had recorded mental health need, highest among Mixed White-Black Caribbean pupils (74.0%). Among those in AP, 52.0% of girls with a mental health-related hospital contact had school provision, compared to 67.3% boys. For some racial-ethnic groups, schools appeared less likely to record need evident in hospital records; 17.5% boys and 36.2% girls from Mixed White-Asian backgrounds enrolled in AP had mental health-related hospital contact without school provision. ConclusionAmong pupils enrolled in AP, documented mental health need is high but unevenly recorded across systems, with inequalities by racial-ethnic group and gender.

papers.title: Stakeholder perspectives and preferences for long-acting injectables for tuberculosis treatment and prevention: a multi-regional mixed-methods study
papers.abstract: ObjectiveTo assess stakeholder acceptability of and preferences for long-acting injectables (LAIs) for tuberculosis (TB) treatment and prevention across World Health Organization regions to inform product development and implementation. MethodsWe conducted a sequential explanatory mixed-methods study of survey data and qualitative focus group discussions (FGDs). Online surveys assessed perceptions and acceptance of LAIs among two groups: TB programme managers, civil society members and healthcare workers (Survey A), and community members and persons affected by TB (Survey B). Using purposive sampling, survey participants were invited to join FGDs to explore survey findings. Survey data were analysed using descriptive statistics, ordinal logistic regression with stepwise AIC selection, and one-sample proportion tests. FGD transcripts were analysed using modified framework analysis. FindingsAmong 310 participants (102 Survey A; 208 Survey B), 83% (n=256) favoured LAIs over standard oral TB treatment. Compared with six months of daily oral treatment, 69% preferred a three-month regimen comprising one month of daily oral treatment followed by four injections per monthly visit for two months, while 80% preferred the corresponding regimen with two injections per visit. For prevention, 79% preferred a single injection over one month of oral treatment. In Survey B, interest varied according to lived TB experience, with FGDs suggesting that previous negative experiences with injectables may have contributed to this variation. ConclusionInterest in LAIs for TB treatment and prevention was high, but lower among participants with lived TB experience. Product development and implementation should address concerns about injectables and side effects while preserving patient choice and agency.
